ideas.title: Stuck in the sand: dig, plank, push, rock it free
ideas.critique: This answers what sank 'Beached' in round 1: the burying comes from a Wong-Reece wheel model in the sand field that already slumps to repose, so getting stuck is the numbers, and digging and planking are hands-on fixes that stay in the sand. It is a lot of coupling for one session (wheel contact arc, dig, plank body, push traction), and if only the sinkage lands, the clip is a cart sitting in a rut. The gust that rocks it out is the vaguest part.

ideas.title: Two wheels up: friends hike out on the rail
ideas.critique: Here the friends' masses really are what holds the cart down, and a capsize with ragdolls thrown by the same rigid step is a clip people would share; that fixes the canned-lean worry from round 1's helmsman pose. The yacht is still not sailable, though, so this depends on the sheet and heel control existing first. Friends sent to fixed deck spots with keys 1-3 is close to a lookup of three positions.

ideas.title: The low-tide sea: a solved flood over a sailing flat
ideas.critique: Swapping round 1's sine-on-a-plane for a wetting-and-drying shallow-water solver is a real step: creeks that flood first and puddles left in hollows would come from the solver and could carry more later. It is a big engine change aimed at a sailing flat for a yacht nobody can sail yet, and the tie to soaked-sand Bekker numbers rests on a saturation-to-parameter mapping that will be typed in.

ideas.title: The dynamo lamp: sail into the dusk and the mast lights up
ideas.critique: EMF from the real flux change, with back-EMF drag that makes light cost speed, is an honest coupling and sits right on the road step of the dynamo charging the pots. But a hot wire glowing by Joule heat is 'Where I rushed it' again on a mast, the clip is another glowing-wire picture from the electric series, and the choice of lamp on or off is thin play.
